title.en: Although it rained, despite the rain

goal.sl: Poveš nasprotje (Although it rained, we walked; despite the rain; however), namen (in order to, so that) in vzrok (because of; as a result).
goal.de: Du sagst einen Gegensatz (Although it rained, we walked; despite the rain; however), einen Zweck (in order to, so that) und einen Grund (because of; as a result).
goal.it: Dici un contrasto (Although it rained, we walked; despite the rain; however), uno scopo (in order to, so that) e una causa (because of; as a result).
goal.en: You can say a contrast (Although it rained, we walked; despite the rain; however), what something is for (in order to, so that) and why (because of; as a result).

say.sl: **although**, **though**, **even though** (čeprav) + stavek. **Although it rained, we walked to the tarn.** (Čeprav je deževalo, smo šli do jezerca.) **We walked, even though it rained.** (Šli smo, čeprav je deževalo.) **even though** je močnejši. Če je veznik prvi, je vejica.
say.de: **although**, **though**, **even though** (obwohl) + Satz. **Although it rained, we walked to the tarn.** (Obwohl es regnete, gingen wir zum Bergsee.) **We walked, even though it rained.** (Wir gingen, obwohl es regnete.) **even though** ist stärker. Steht es vorn, kommt ein Komma.
say.it: **although**, **though**, **even though** (anche se, sebbene) + una frase. **Although it rained, we walked to the tarn.** (Anche se pioveva, siamo andati al laghetto.) **We walked, even though it rained.** (Siamo andati, anche se pioveva.) **even though** è più forte. Se viene prima, c'è la virgola.
say.en: **although**, **though**, **even though** + a sentence. **Although it rained, we walked to the tarn.** **We walked, even though it rained.** **even though** is stronger. With it first, there is a comma.

examples.en: Although it rained, we walked to the tarn.
examples.sl: Čeprav je deževalo, smo šli do jezerca.
examples.de: Obwohl es regnete, gingen wir zum Bergsee.
examples.it: Anche se pioveva, siamo andati al laghetto.

examples.en: We walked, even though it rained.
Though it was cold, we sat outside.
examples.sl: Čeprav je bilo mrzlo, smo sedeli zunaj.
examples.de: Obwohl es kalt war, saßen wir draußen.
examples.it: Anche se faceva freddo, siamo stati fuori.

say.sl: Ena veznica je dovolj: **Although it rained, we walked.** Slovenščina lahko reče *čeprav …, pa …*, angleščina nima zraven but. Ali **although** ali **but**: **It rained, but we walked.** (Deževalo je, a smo šli.)
say.de: Ein Bindewort genügt: **Although it rained, we walked.** Englisch setzt kein but dazu. Entweder **although** oder **but**: **It rained, but we walked.** (Es regnete, aber wir gingen.)
say.it: Basta una congiunzione: **Although it rained, we walked.** L'italiano può dire *anche se …, però …*, l'inglese non aggiunge but. O **although** o **but**: **It rained, but we walked.** (Pioveva, ma siamo andati.)
say.en: One joining word is enough: **Although it rained, we walked.** English adds no but. Either **although** or **but**: **It rained, but we walked.**

so we walked to the tarn.

explain.de:

explain.it:

explain.en:

say.sl: **despite** in **in spite of** (kljub) + samostalnik ali -ing, ne stavek: **Despite the rain, we walked.** (Kljub dežju smo šli.) **In spite of the snow, the bus came.** (Kljub snegu je avtobus prišel.) **Despite feeling ill, she came.** (Čeprav ji ni bilo dobro, je prišla.) Za **despite** ni of, **in spite of** ga ima.
say.de: **despite** und **in spite of** (trotz) + Nomen oder -ing, kein Satz: **Despite the rain, we walked.** (Trotz des Regens gingen wir.) **In spite of the snow, the bus came.** (Trotz des Schnees kam der Bus.) **Despite feeling ill, she came.** (Obwohl sie sich krank fühlte, kam sie.) Nach **despite** kein of, **in spite of** hat es.
say.it: **despite** e **in spite of** (nonostante) + un nome o -ing, non una frase: **Despite the rain, we walked.** (Nonostante la pioggia, siamo andati.) **In spite of the snow, the bus came.** (Nonostante la neve, l'autobus è arrivato.) **Despite feeling ill, she came.** (Anche se non stava bene, è venuta.) Dopo **despite** niente of, **in spite of** ce l'ha.
say.en: **despite** and **in spite of** + a noun or -ing, not a sentence: **Despite the rain, we walked.** **In spite of the snow, the bus came.** **Despite feeling ill, she came.** No of after **despite**; **in spite of** has it.

examples.en: In spite of the snow, the bus came.
examples.de: Trotz des Schnees kam der Bus.
examples.it: Nonostante la neve, l'autobus è arrivato.

examples.sl: Čeprav ji ni bilo dobro, je prišla.
examples.de: Obwohl sie sich krank fühlte, kam sie.
examples.it: Anche se non stava bene, è venuta.

say.sl: **however** (vendar) začne nov stavek, z vejico: **It rained. However, we walked.** (Deževalo je, vendar smo šli.) To je bolj pisno. V govoru **though** na koncu: **We walked, though.** (Pa smo vseeno šli.) **but** poveže dva dela istega stavka.
say.de: **however** (jedoch) beginnt einen neuen Satz, mit Komma: **It rained. However, we walked.** (Es regnete, trotzdem gingen wir.) Das klingt eher geschrieben. Gesprochen **though** am Ende: **We walked, though.** (Wir gingen aber trotzdem.) **but** verbindet zwei Teile eines Satzes.
say.it: **however** (tuttavia) comincia una frase nuova, con la virgola: **It rained. However, we walked.** (Pioveva, tuttavia siamo andati.) È più da scritto. A voce **though** alla fine: **We walked, though.** (Però siamo andati.) **but** unisce due parti della stessa frase.
say.en: **however** starts a new sentence, with a comma: **It rained. However, we walked.** It's more for writing. In talk, **though** at the end: **We walked, though.** **but** joins two parts of one sentence.

explain.en:

- It was late. However, Mrs Birkett made us some soup.

say.sl: Namen: **to** ali **in order to** (da bi) + osnovna oblika: **Jack got up early in order to feed the sheep.** (Jack je zgodaj vstal, da bi nahranil ovce.) **so that** + stavek s can, could, will, would: **I left early so that I could catch the bus.** (Zgodaj sem {m:šel|f:šla}, da bi {m:ujel|f:ujela} avtobus.) V govoru tudi samo **so**: *so I could catch the bus*.
say.de: Zweck: **to** oder **in order to** (um zu) + Grundform: **Jack got up early in order to feed the sheep.** (Jack stand früh auf, um die Schafe zu füttern.) **so that** (damit) + Satz mit can, could, will, would: **I left early so that I could catch the bus.** (Ich ging früh, damit ich den Bus erwischte.) Gesprochen auch nur **so**: *so I could catch the bus*.
say.it: Lo scopo: **to** o **in order to** (per) + la forma base: **Jack got up early in order to feed the sheep.** (Jack si è alzato presto per dare da mangiare alle pecore.) **so that** (così che) + una frase con can, could, will, would: **I left early so that I could catch the bus.** (Sono partit{m:o|f:a} presto per prendere l'autobus.) A voce anche solo **so**: *so I could catch the bus*.
say.en: What for: **to** or **in order to** + the base form: **Jack got up early in order to feed the sheep.** **so that** + a sentence with can, could, will, would: **I left early so that I could catch the bus.** In talk also just **so**: *so I could catch the bus*.

say.sl: Vzrok: **because** + stavek, **because of** (zaradi) + samostalnik: **We stayed because it snowed.** (Ostali smo, ker je snežilo.) **We stayed because of the snow.** (Zaradi snega smo ostali.) Kar je sledilo: **as a result** (zato), na začetku novega stavka: **The road was closed. As a result, the bus didn't come.** (Cesta je bila zaprta, zato avtobus ni prišel.)
say.de: Grund: **because** (weil) + Satz, **because of** (wegen) + Nomen: **We stayed because it snowed.** (Wir blieben, weil es schneite.) **We stayed because of the snow.** (Wir blieben wegen des Schnees.) Was folgte: **as a result** (infolgedessen), am Anfang eines neuen Satzes: **The road was closed. As a result, the bus didn't come.** (Die Straße war gesperrt, darum kam der Bus nicht.)
say.it: La causa: **because** (perché) + una frase, **because of** (a causa di) + un nome: **We stayed because it snowed.** (Siamo rimasti perché nevicava.) **We stayed because of the snow.** (Siamo rimasti per la neve.) Ciò che è seguito: **as a result** (di conseguenza), all'inizio di una frase nuova: **The road was closed. As a result, the bus didn't come.** (La strada era chiusa, perciò l'autobus non è arrivato.)
say.en: Why: **because** + a sentence, **because of** + a noun: **We stayed because it snowed.** **We stayed because of the snow.** What followed: **as a result**, at the start of a new sentence: **The road was closed. As a result, the bus didn't come.**

translation.sl: Čeprav je bila nevihta huda, je šel Jack na hrib iskat ovce. Kljub vetru jih je našel večino. Vendar je manjkalo jagnje. Ostal je zunaj do teme, da bi ga našel. Cesta je bila zaprta zaradi podrtega drevesa, zato je šel domov peš. Posledično je zamudil na ples.
translation.de: Obwohl der Sturm schlimm war, ging Jack auf den Berg, um seine Schafe zu suchen. Trotz des Windes fand er die meisten. Aber ein Lamm fehlte. Er blieb bis zur Dunkelheit draußen, damit er es finden konnte. Die Straße war wegen eines umgestürzten Baums gesperrt, also ging er zu Fuß heim. Darum kam er zu spät zum Tanz.
translation.it: Anche se il temporale era forte, Jack è salito sul monte a cercare le pecore. Nonostante il vento, ha trovato quasi tutte. Tuttavia mancava un agnello. È rimasto fuori fino a buio per trovarlo. La strada era chiusa per un albero caduto, così è tornato a piedi. Di conseguenza è arrivato tardi al ballo.
translation.en: Although the storm was bad, Jack went up the fell to look for his sheep. Despite the wind, he found most of them. However, a lamb was missing. He stayed out till dark so that he could find it. The road was closed because of a fallen tree, so he walked home. As a result, he was late for the dance.
